A manual review covered 240 mentions of historical people. At the current threshold of 0.72, precision is 0.86 and recall is 0.79. The most common errors involve common surnames, initials without a full first name, and honorifics such as “D.” or “Dña.” being interpreted as part of the name.

The recommended automatic-acceptance threshold is 0.78. Candidates between 0.60 and 0.78 would undergo human review, while those below 0.60 would remain unlinked unless there is an additional match on date, profession, or location. This policy reduces incorrect links, although it will increase the review workload.

Diego will repeat the evaluation after normalizing honorifics and spelling variants. Mateo will prepare a list of 30 difficult cases. The report must clearly separate automatic precision, results after human review, and mentions that remain without an assigned entity.
